analytic_obligations.check: g is Kähler, h is an arbitrary positive Hermitian tangent metric; the fixed ambient compact setting and n>=2 are explicit.
Unscaled bundle curvature, holomorphic sectional curvature, Ricci form and scalar trace operator use mutually consistent signs.
The normalized complex Gaussian density has second moment1 and fourth moment2.
Independence and coordinate phase symmetry give both Kronecker contractions, with2 when all indices coincide.
Expected quartic curvature is Q+B without using Kähler symmetries of h.
Expected fourth metric norm is u squared plus q, including non-diagonal positive matrices by unitary invariance.
The negative sectional bound gives the factor one half for the symmetrized trace.
Both curvature contractions are real and invariant under unitary frame changes.
The difference of Chern connections is tensorial and g has zero torsion, so its skew part is precisely h torsion.
The mixed tensor norm uses g on both input slots and h on the output slot.
Symmetric and skew tensors are orthogonal, giving the quarter torsion norm.
The second-derivative four-term tensor is the coefficient of the unscaled i d dbar omega_h with holomorphic differentials first.
In a unitary frame the wedge product and contraction differ by exactly2, including n=2 and zero-th omega power.
Closedness of omega_g makes the exact-form integral vanish; no closedness of omega_h is used.
Antisymmetrizing the four curvature terms gives minus D plus the h-torsion square.
Contracting the antisymmetrization gives2(Q-B)=torsion norm squared minus D_g.
Solving for Q gives symmetrized trace plus one quarter torsion norm minus one quarter D_g.
Kähler-normal holomorphic coordinates make first derivatives of g vanish.
The inverse-metric second-derivative term is the Ricci-h contraction by the curvature symmetries of g alone.
The h second-derivative term is minus Q plus the connection-difference norm squared.
Combining norm splitting and curvature symmetrization cancels the torsion terms and leaves plus D_g/4.
The scalar Laplacian has zero integral with respect to the Kähler volume.
All three terms in the integrated identity are continuous and nonnegative when Ricci(g)>=0 and H_h<=0.
Their zero integrals imply pointwise zero terms.
Positive h pairs strictly positively with any nonzero semipositive Ricci matrix, forcing Ricci(g)=0.
Zero Gaussian expectation of a nonpositive continuous quartic with everywhere positive density forces every directional value to vanish.
Vanishing directional holomorphic sectional curvature excludes quasi-negativity; no full Chern tensor flatness is inferred.
RC-positivity on the prior Ricci-flat surface uses independent tangent/fiber directions and remains compatible with this obstruction.
